coverage_notes: Bonferroni (Prop. bonf): no defect. Truncation direction checked for both functionals. Corr_1 <= S0-S1+S2 (even truncation), so J_T >= J-(S0-S1+S2)-Corr2. ∫_V P^2 >= S'0-S'1 (odd truncation), so I_T <= I-S'0+S'1. Corr_2 (integrand Q(R)^2-Q(U)^2, no sign) is kept in full, so its lack of sign does not matter. The identity Σ_{j<=l}(-1)^j C(N,j) = (-1)^l C(N-1,l) holds. G_A >= 0 and the partition by exact large set A are correct. The proposed Open step (split Corr_2 into its Q(R)^2 and Q(U_A)^2 parts with U_A defined from s_A) is viable.

Recomputed from code/cap6/res_kin48_D22r.json + pieces_kin48_D22r.jsonl, independently of compare_two_programs.py: piece sums reproduce Corr1, Icorr, Corr2b, Corr2c, I_T and J_T exactly; 48 J_T/I_T = 4.006081420810689; one-sided 48 J_low/I_up = 4.006081420807216 > 4 (exact comparison); loss 3.47e-12; omitted pieces 4.31 of 15.52 core-hours (27.8%); 46 Corr1 + 50 Icorr = 96 pieces; with the 46 Corr1 of SY, 142 pieces, all with sign (-1)^j (Corr2b/Corr2c pieces also alternate). SY Corr_1 levels 2.32e-6, -1.66e-10, 6.96e-20, -2.50e-69 of J agree; Corr_2/J 2.42e-4.

Song–Yue: witness table has 1295 rows, all parts even, max degree 25; converted file 1311 terms. compare_sy236.json and compare2_sy236.json give exact equality with Iref (655 digits) and Jref (715 digits), and the factors 10^192/10^196 x 5^150 521^50 match the t-coordinate normalisation in songyue_compare.py. Ratios 1.000664921591 / 4.0026596864 / 4.0030988047 / 4.0036348167 and I_T/I_0 = 0.99989031 confirmed. I verified (no repository script records this) that the cap-free I, J of capped_exact.py --jonly equal I0, J0 of songyue_I0/J0.py exactly. The fields ratio_capped_I_T_* of compare_sy236_exact.json equal the cap-free-denominator ratio (jonly has I_T = I); this is harmless but may confuse readers. songyue_pointcheck.py uses points with t_i in {0..60}/10^4, a weak Schwartz–Zippel set for degree 25; the conversion is nevertheless confirmed by the exact I0/J0 and Jref equalities.

Kintali: parameters (L, τ, g, C, U) and the dilation 520/521 verified. Max m and j in the pieces files match (Icorr m <= 14, Corr1 m <= 13, j <= 3). Cap-free certificates: D22 Rayleigh 3.958904638305 x 253/250 = 4.006411494; D20 gives 3.99943 < 4. The caps cost 0.00033.

v0.8: opt49 4.0124198475 by both programs (exact I_T, J_T equal); regained 0.000381 of 0.004137 (9.2%); k=45 regained 0.01186 of 0.038585 (30.7%). Gram/PD logic checked (see P4-S6B-10). Logs show CEILING 4 and 3.99 True (v0.9 recheck) and 3.985 False (v0.8), which is consistent with the optimum 3.98555.

Hybrid floor: monotonicity in k is justified at full-source line 600. Reduction steps checked (c1, c2, K >= 0; scaling factor 4; the ε<0 remark). Ran floor_hybrid.py --check (mpmath.iv) on all five cert_floor_hybrid_*.json: all OK, with contiguous coverage to A and assertions a >= s1 > τ, s1 <= L. Spot check: for k=27, ω=0.007 the floating-point sup W first reaches 4 at ε ≈ 0.055, consistent with the remark.

Rung 186: (2.34)-(2.35) arithmetic re-verified exactly. The closed form of ρ_D on [2,3] was checked by differentiation and quadrature. Only the cell-count and width slips were found (P4-S6B-04). Remark sta-lemma5 and the 186 source descriptions are Literature readings; no source access (no internet), so they were not checked.

findings.title: The lower end 3.98555 of the claimed interval for the Lemma 9.1 optimum is rounded up past the attained value
findings.location: 'The optimum' paragraph after Prop. prop:cha-ceiling; section file 006 line 474 (paper/main.tex line 1349)
findings.quote: ($3.97369$) is beaten by $0.0119$, the best possible lies in
findings.claim: The best possible capped ratio in V for the Lemma 9.1 caps lies in [3.98555, 3.99).
findings.issue: The value actually attained is 3.98554779524..., which is below 3.98555. So the stated lower endpoint is not a lower bound. The endpoint also comes from floating-point Gram matrices and was not re-certified exactly, which the same paragraph admits.
findings.analysis: runs/gram45_lemma91_recheck.log: inverse iteration converges to [3.98554779524011 +/- 4.30e-15], and code/cap6/P_opt45_lemma91_D21r_u.json has gram_ratio '[3.98554779524011 +/- 4.30e-15]'. Inverse iteration with shift 4.3 converges to the eigenvalue nearest 4.3, so this value is (numerically) the top eigenvalue: the supremum is about 3.9855478 < 3.98555. Rounding to 5 decimals is fine for a point value, but not for the lower end of an interval asserted to contain the optimum. The same rounding feeds Remark rem:prediction ('the optimum 3.98555').
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'lies in [3.98554, 3.99)' (or '(3.985547, 3.99)'), and say that the left end is a floating-point value of a rounded vector. Alternatively certify it with capped_check.py on P_opt45_lemma91_D21r_u.json.

findings.title: The 'second-order picture' predicts a gain of about 0.033, below the loss 0.0386, not above it
findings.location: Remark rem:prediction; section file 006 line 492 (paper/main.tex line 1367)
findings.quote: the gap fitted at $k=49$, would instead predict a gain larger than the loss
findings.claim: A pure second-order model (gain ~ loss^2/gap, gap fitted at k=49) would predict a gain larger than the loss at k=45.
findings.issue: With the natural reading the prediction is smaller than the loss.
findings.analysis: At k=49: loss = 4.0161761 - 4.0120389035 = 0.0041372, gain = 4.0124198475 - 4.0120389035 = 0.00038094, so gap = loss^2/gain = 0.044932. At k=45 (Lemma 9.1): loss = 4.012272 - 3.9736869862 = 0.038585, so the predicted gain is loss^2/gap = 0.03313, which is 86% of the loss, not more than it. (Equivalently gain_45 = gain_49 (loss_45/loss_49)^2 = 0.0331.) Only a mixed convention, with the gap fitted using cap-free minus optimum (0.003756) at k=49 but the truncation loss used at k=45, gives about 0.040 > 0.0386. The remark's conclusion, that the heuristic is ruled out because 0.0119 is far from either prediction, is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Numbers from Prop. prop:opt49, Thm. thm:capped-exact, Prop. prop:capfree, Prop. prop:cha-ceiling and the 'optimum' paragraph; notes/session8-prediction.md (no computation of the second-order prediction is recorded there or in log/entries.json).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with 'would predict a gain of about 0.033, nearly the whole loss', or state the convention that gives a gain above the loss.

findings.title: Section disclaims what its first part asserts and the source notes confirm: V equals Charton et al.'s B_21
findings.location: paragraph after 'The optimum' (Prop. prop:cha-ceiling); compare line 57 (main.tex 932); section file 006 line 483 (paper/main.tex line 1358)
findings.quote: is the same as ours (only the dimension is equal), so this is a located
findings.claim: We have not checked that their space is the same as ours (only the dimension is equal).
findings.issue: Line 57 of the same section says 'our degree-$21$ basis is the space $\mathcal B_{21}$ of \cite[Thm.~11.1]{Cha26}'. notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md quotes Cha26 §11 directly: 'B21 = spanQ {(L − P1)^a Pλ : a ≥ 0, λj ∈ 2Z>0, a + |λ| ≤ 21}' with P_λ a product of power sums. That is exactly the space V of Prop. prop:cha-ceiling. The paper therefore disclaims a fact it states and has checked. This also undersells the consequence: if the support and fiber formula agree too (the notes quote U(x̂)=min{L−S, max{g, C(s+1)−ρ1}}, which matches Prop. prop:exact(1)), then Prop. prop:cha-ceiling shows, up to the stated failure probability and the reliance on capped_check.py, that no F in B_21 reaches 4.00438 with Lemma 9.1's caps.
findings.analysis: This duplicates P3-S6A-02, filed from the other locator. It is recorded here because the consequential sentence sits in this slice.
findings.evidence: Section lines 55-58 vs 482-485; notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md lines 192-199; notes/sources-enlarged-supports.md lines 251-252.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one statement. Either say the spaces agree by definition (cite the quoted §11 definition) and that the remaining unchecked points are the support and fiber conventions, or withdraw the line-57 assertion.

findings.title: kintali_extra_le_three covers only cap-violation pieces, not the Corr_2 pieces it is cited for
findings.location: Kintali paragraph; section file 006 line 509 (paper/main.tex line 1384)
findings.claim: Every correction piece has j ≤ 3 (Lean-checked: kintali_extra_le_three).
findings.issue: The Lean lemma assumes hs : 1899 < s, a large set above the cap (Corr_1 and ∫_V P^2 pieces). The Corr_2 pieces have admissible u' with s ≤ C, and there j ≤ 3 comes from jg < L − C (Corr2c: ρ < L − C_{m+1} − jg; Corr2b: s ≥ C − g and |u'| < L − g), which the lemma does not cover. Like the other counting lemmas, it is also stated for lists of naturals in units of 1/2500, not for real coordinates (see P3-S6A-04). The fact itself is true: 4·182 = 728 > 706 = 2605 − 1899, and the data show max j = 3 for all kinds.
findings.analysis: lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean lines 94-98 (docstring: 'In a cap-violation piece the large set carries more than 1899'). code/cap6/pieces_kin48_D22r.jsonl and pieces_sy236_jonly.jsonl have max j = 3 for Corr2b and Corr2c.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the one-line real argument for the Corr_2 pieces (jg < L − C), or add a Lean lemma with hypothesis s + l.sum < 2605 − 1899 + s, and state that the Lean facts are integer-unit analogues.

findings.title: Ceiling certificate's status label omits that it is probabilistic and single-program, and its exact weights are not archived
findings.location: Proposition prop:cha-ceiling header; section file 006 line 431 (paper/main.tex line 1306)
findings.issue: The ball-arithmetic part is sound; I checked the code. But the identification of the Gram forms with the capped functionals rests on one Schwartz–Zippel test (failure probability below 2^-31 per functional, pseudo-random point from Python random.Random(20261113)) and on capped_check.py alone at these caps. The exact weights used for both the PD test and the random-point test were loaded from /tmp/claude-0/w45_lemma91.pkl, which is not in the repository. So the certificate cannot be re-checked without rerunning the 88-minute adjoint. The body text discloses the probabilistic and single-program reliance, but the label does not.
findings.analysis: Checked in code/capped_gram.py. Hfix = floor(w·2^P) has error in [0,1) per weight. The entrywise radius colabs[t1]·colabs[t2]+1 bounds the propagated error of Q^T H Q with integer Q. arb(int) is exact (tested with python-flint 0.9.0). is_pd uses the rigorous arb_mat.solve, uses M21 = M12^T (valid because GJint and G_I are exactly symmetric), takes the union symmetrisation, and has the base case M[0,0] > 0. So the PD step is rigorous given the weights. runs/gram45_rand_selftest.log and gram45_lemma91_recheck.log both say 'weights loaded from /tmp/claude-0/w45_lemma91.pkl'. P_rand45_lemma91_u.json has 846 nonzero integer coefficients in [−2^31, 2^31], so |S| = 2^32+1 as claimed.
findings.evidence: code/capped_gram.py (gram, is_pd, main); runs/gram45_rand_selftest.log; runs/gram45_lemma91_recheck.log; code/cap6/P_rand45_lemma91_u.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Label it 'Computed, ball arithmetic; identification of the Gram forms probabilistic (Schwartz–Zippel) and via capped_check.py only'. Archive the weights pickle (or its hash) alongside the logs.
